shorts.hook: Brown On Impeaching Trump: 'I Would Not'

claims.text: Sherrod Brown, a Democrat running for his Ohio Senate seat, said he would not support impeaching President Trump, telling the Columbus Dispatch on Oct. 9.
Brown is quoted: "I can't speak for everybody else, but I would not support an impeachment of Trump."
In Trump's first term Brown voted to convict him after both House impeachments.
RedState's Oct. 14 column quotes Brown as saying "We're, you know, obviously not confirming judges that are Trump judges."

shorts.title: Trump-Nominated Judge Keeps CNN, MS NOW, Politico In White House #Shorts
shorts.hook: A Trump-Nominated Judge Rules Against Trump
shorts.narration: [deadpan] Folks, the White House tried to bar reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico. Then it ran into Judge Timothy Kelly. [beat] Per PBS, Kelly was nominated by Trump himself. [amused] Talk about hiring the wrong guy. On Tuesday he extended his order blocking the ban, finding the outlets likely to win on First Amendment and due process claims. Seventy-eight reporters were affected. [sarcastic] Seventy-eight reporters, friends, desperate to get back to asking questions. Government lawyers argued, quote, "access to the White House is a privilege — not a right." [beat] The judge wasn't buying it. Proverbs says, "The lip of truth shall be established for ever: but a lying tongue is but for a moment." Maybe the White House should appeal, folks. Does a president get to pick his own press corps, yes or no? Tell me below. subscribe, Henry roasts the news every day.

claims.text: U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, nominated by Trump, extended an order blocking the administration from barring reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, issuing a preliminary injunction on Tuesday, Oct. 13, 2026.
Kelly found the outlets likely to succeed on their free speech and due process claims.
The bans affected 78 reporters across the three outlets.
Government lawyers argued "access to the White House is a privilege — not a right."
